claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy has a multiphase lamellar or interpenetrating microstructure with distinct phase boundaries.
Homogenization or post-processing can reduce distinct eutectic phase boundaries while preserving the overall alloy composition.
Eutectic phase boundaries are preferential sites for localized oxidation.
The phase boundaries facilitate localized galvanic coupling between the coexisting phases.
The coexisting phases have differential oxidation kinetics.
Differential oxidation preferentially forms brittle oxide layers along phase boundaries.
Mechanical loading causes the interfacial brittle oxide layers to lose integrity and spall.
Spallation of the oxide layers generates abrasive debris.
The generated oxide debris increases wear by promoting abrasive material removal.
Oxide spallation exposes fresh reactive alloy surfaces and thereby accelerates corrosion.
The interactions among oxidation, spallation, abrasive debris, wear, and renewed surface exposure create a self-accelerating degradation process.
Relative to the homogenized baseline, the eutectic microstructure will have a higher total degradation rate.
Relative to the homogenized baseline, the eutectic microstructure will have a higher wear rate because of abrasive oxide debris.
Relative to the homogenized baseline, the eutectic microstructure will have a higher corrosion rate associated with localized interphase oxidation and galvanic effects.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate at temperatures of at least approximately 400°C in an aggressive oxidizing or chloride-containing environment under mechanically significant wear.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at lower temperatures or in environments lacking an aggressive oxidizing agent.
A matched comparison under identical temperature, environment, load, and sliding conditions can distinguish the effect of distinct eutectic phase boundaries.

The phase-boundary mechanism is to be rejected if the eutectic sample shows no statistically significant increases in both wear and corrosion relative to the baseline and no preferential boundary oxidation or spallation is observed.
